- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) and forecast is high, apply downward bias of 3–7% to reflect mean reversion.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), reduce subsequent forecast values by 2–5% to correct for overreaction.  
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and forecast is trending upward, cap the slope to avoid overfitting to recent momentum.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early mean reversion (first 5–7 days), adjust forecast downward by 1–3% to align with sentiment-driven correction.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated negative swings, model should not overcorrect upward — apply a “sentiment lag” rule: forecast should not exceed 20% above recent 7-day average unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
